items.title: 52263_Sonny Greer oral history interview
items.q: And a friend of mine, Fizol's wife, say they ain't going to let you try on no hat.

ctx.x: You say that the City of Washington itself, the racial prejudices didn't break down until --

The second World War, because they was bringing government workers and different people working with government from all over the United States, so naturally they had to break down, because the colored was working down there The chick? was down wasn't no colored people go downtown in Washington and sit in no restaurant, go in a store and buy a hat. You couldn't go in there and buy a suit. I mean, try it on, you couldn't try no shoes on, hats, because my wife she wasn't used to that.
And a friend of mine, Fizol's wife, say they ain't going to let you try on no hat. My wife --
